gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a trail camera's PIR motion sensor fires only on a heat difference between the animal and the background, crossing its detection zones. GardePro puts mammals at about 98°F, so on a 90°F day there is little contrast and the camera can miss animals in range. GardePro also says the sensor is most sensitive to sideways movement and that an animal walking straight at the camera delays the trigger.
standout_why: I read Outdoor Life (Best Trail Cameras 2026), TechGearLab (Best Trail Cameras 2026) and Field & Stream (Best Cellular Trail Cameras). All three cover detection range and trigger speed but never explain what the sensor responds to. None mentions PIR, heat contrast, hot-weather misses, or crossing versus head-on approach. TechGearLab only notes that the GardePro A3S has a 'large detection zone' and that Moultrie's Smart Zones can exclude areas. Field & Stream only says farther objects must be larger to be detected. Wirecutter (blocked directly and via the proxy), Popular Mechanics (fetch refused) and Digital Camera World (body truncated) could not be read, so I can't rule out that one of them covers it.
decides: This doesn't change which camera ChatGPT picked, but it decides whether 'motion activated' works for this shopper. Every candidate triggers on heat, not on motion as such, so a fast trigger like the 0.2 s on the Bushnell or 0.1 s on the GardePro A3S can't help when an animal walks straight at the lens on a hot afternoon. Mount the camera at about 45° to the trail, set sensitivity to High in hot weather and Medium/Low in wind, and prefer models that list a PIR detection angle wider than the lens field of view (GardePro's '120° Wide Detection' side sensors). That makes the A3S, with 3 PIR sensors, a sound budget pick.

findings.label: What a PIR trail-camera sensor detects
findings.value: Temperature difference (Delta T) between a moving warm body and the background, crossing sensor zones
findings.source_title: Trail Camera PIR Sensors Explained: Range, Angles, and Sensitivity Guide (GardePro, NguyenHien, 2025-12-08)
findings.note: Maker's words: 'PIR sensors function by detecting the temperature difference (Delta T) between a moving object and the background'; 'When a warm-blooded animal moves across these zones, the sensor registers a change in infrared voltage.'

findings.label: Hot-weather contrast loss
findings.value: Mammal body about 98°F (37°C) vs background on a 90°F (32°C) day: about 8°F (5°C) of contrast
findings.note: GardePro: 'On a hot day (e.g., 90°F / 32°C), the background temperature is very close to the animal's body temperature.' The 8°F / 5°C difference is my subtraction of the two figures GardePro gives. GardePro advises: 'In high-temperature environments, increase the sensitivity setting.'

findings.label: Direction of travel
findings.value: Most sensitive to sideways (lateral) movement; movement straight toward the camera delays the trigger
findings.note: Maker's words: 'PIR sensors are most sensitive to lateral movement.' 'If a subject moves directly toward the trail camera, it delays the trigger signal.' Recommends mounting at about 45° to the trail.

findings.label: PIR detection angle vs lens field of view
findings.note: Maker's words: 'Trail camera specifications often list detection angles that differ from the lens field of view (FOV).' Models with '120° Wide Detection' add side sensors that wake the camera before an animal reaches the central zone.

findings.label: Trigger condition (second maker)
findings.value: Motion AND heat both required; hot weather makes the PIR react less sensitively
findings.source_title: PIR sensor and trigger sensitivity (Burrel Cameras support)
findings.note: Maker's words: 'The camera's PIR sensor responds if it detects motion AND heat in front of the camera.' 'hot weather make the PIR sensor react less sensitively.' Recommends the Low setting in winter and freezing conditions.

findings.label: PIR sensors / trigger speed / price
findings.source_title: GardePro A3S Non-Cellular Trail Camera (GardePro US store)
findings.note: From storecheck.py on the GardePro Shopify store: '0.1s Ultra-Fast Trigger: 3 PIR sensors'; price $71.99, in stock. The compare-at price of $695.99 is ignored as not credible.
